name: Marble
summary: Marble turns text, a single image or a video clip into a persistent, navigable 3D environment that can be edited and exported, rather than into a video that exists only as pixels. The distinction is the whole point of World Labs' spatial-intelligence thesis: the output is scene geometry — point clouds and Gaussian splats — so it can be re-rendered from any viewpoint, imported into a simulator and interacted with, instead of being a fixed camera path. It is the first world model commercialised as a general product, and the substrate World Labs' later robotics work is built on.
innovation: Emits persistent 3D geometry rather than video frames, so the generated world survives being looked at from a new angle.
Made world models a product with an export path into existing 3D and simulation tooling.
matters: Established the generated-scene-as-asset pattern that the real-to-sim robotics pipeline later depends on.
limits: Commercial product with no paper or weights; architecture details are not public.
Scene generation quality is the selling point; physical fidelity of the resulting worlds is not characterised.
lineage: Generative interactive environments in the Genie tradition, redirected from playable video to exportable 3D geometry.
